objections.claim: The native-launcher mechanism is internally contradictory and its oracle would not establish the claimed property. Its closed syscall grammar admits only environment clearing, open/fstat/read/close, exec-family calls, and process control, but the required sealed snapshot necessarily uses memfd_create, writes/copies bytes into the memfd, fcntl(F_ADD_SEALS), and normally seeks or maps data; the approach later explicitly says the launcher calls memfd_create/fcntl. Moreover, no PT_INTERP/DT_NEEDED plus a source scan for named socket calls does not prove a statically linked binary contains no reachable indirect or compiler/runtime syscall path. Double-building proves reproducibility, not correspondence to the reviewed syscall grammar. The plan must define an implementable syscall set and a discriminating enforcement mechanism over the executed artifact—such as a freestanding closed linked closure plus runtime syscall denial or another sound whole-binary verifier—with regressions for indirect/linked listener syscalls.

The external-tool exception still defeats the no-listener guarantee. `bwrap --unshare-net` creates an isolated network namespace; it does not prohibit socket(), bind(), or listen(), so a Git descendant can open a listener while the plan's claimed categorical containment and “no listener opens” regression appear green if they observe only the host namespace. In addition, sealing and hashing a dynamically linked node/git executable authenticates only its main ELF bytes: fexecve subsequently loads the PT_INTERP and DT_NEEDED closure from mutable host paths, outside the recorded digest and source grammar, where pre-main code can open a listener. The plan must either kernel-deny listener syscalls for the complete descendant/runtime closure and bind every executable loader/library byte, or explicitly freeze and authenticate that platform closure as a trust root; add private-namespace-listener and substituted-loader/DT_NEEDED regressions.
